paper.title_en: TWIN-1: A new 185 to 350 MHz Two-Element Radio Interferometer for Solar Observation at Gauribidanur
paper.abstract_en: We present details of a new two-element radio interferometer, namely the TWIN, developed for routine monitoring of solar events at the Gauribidanur Observatory (77.428°E, 13.603°N) between 185 MHz and 350 MHz. This interferometer is built using custom-built antennas, an indigenous RF front-end consisting of LNAs, power combiners, and high-gain amplifiers, and RF over fiber signal transport modules. A data capture system was developed using a commercial digital storage oscilloscope and controlled with custom-designed Python-based tools. The oscilloscope digitises the RF signals with a time resolution of 0.8 ns, bursts of 9952 time samples, with a nominal duty cycle of 3 seconds, and the resultant data is collected on a remote computer. Specialised tools were developed to analyse the data and detect solar events. The interferometer has been operational since July 2023. In our analysis, we have detected several solar events from the ongoing Solar Cycle 25. This paper outlines the design philosophy, signal flow, commissioning and validation, results from a solar event, and future plans for data capture, data analysis, and archival.
